meta.name: ai-sdk-docs-bot-evals-v7-hard-2
meta.notes: 88 answerable + 5 unanswerable. Replaces the first v7-hard set, which scored 94-97%. Built to be harder for retrieval: symptom-phrased questions that don't name the API, precise defaults buried in long pages, cross-page questions, false premises, and near-miss unanswerables where adjacent content tempts invention. Covers error handling, settings, useChat, streaming data, resumable streams, structured output, middleware, providers, testing, agents/subagents/WorkflowAgent, tools, context, telemetry/DevTools, images, reranking, smoothStream. Extra fields: 'topic' and 'difficulty_predicted' (easy/medium/hard) to compare predicted vs actual difficulty. anc-01 and anc-02 failed in the previous run and are kept as anchors. References were written from the live docs on 2026-11-06 (bot snapshot: 2026-11-01). Predicted accuracy with easy=95%, medium=75%, hard=45%: 65%.

questions.question: My streamText API route never throws, even when the provider returns a 500. The try/catch around the streamText(...) call does nothing. Where do these errors go and how do I handle them?
expected_answer: streamText does not throw at call time; errors surface while the stream is consumed
When iterating result.stream, errors arrive as parts with type 'error' (alongside 'abort' and 'tool-error') handled in a switch on part.type
For simple text streams, wrap the for-await loop over textStream in try/catch
An onError callback on streamText also receives the errors

questions.question: Sometimes the provider sends an 'overloaded' error event after streaming has already started. maxRetries doesn't seem to help. How do I retry those failures?
expected_answer: maxRetries only covers failures when starting a model call
Use streamRetries for provider error events received after streaming has begun; stream retries are disabled when it is omitted
Each retry reruns only the failed step; completed earlier steps are not replayed
onError can return { retry: true } to request recovery

questions.question: After enabling stream retries, users occasionally see the first sentence of an answer twice. Is this a bug?
expected_answer: It's documented behavior: text, reasoning, files or sources emitted before the error cannot be retracted
A retry can therefore append duplicate or divergent output to what was already streamed
Open text/reasoning parts are ended before recovered output starts; the failed attempt's output is excluded from the step result, response messages and structured-output parsing

questions.question: When a user cancels a streamText call through an AbortSignal, my onEnd callback never runs, so I lose my usage logging. Which callback should I use?
expected_answer: onEnd does not run when the stream is aborted
Use onAbort, which runs on abort and receives the steps completed before the abort
Alternatively handle the part with type 'abort' in the stream

questions.question: How do I tell whether a provider error that happened mid-stream is worth retrying?
expected_answer: Check StreamProviderError.isInstance(error)
It exposes isRetryable, plus statusCode, code, type and message

questions.question: How many times does generateText retry a failed request by default, and how do I disable retries?
expected_answer: maxRetries defaults to 2
Set maxRetries: 0 to disable retries

questions.question: I want streamText to give up if the model stalls for more than 10 seconds after it started producing output, while allowing the whole call up to 5 minutes. How do I configure that?
expected_answer: Use the timeout option as an object
totalMs: 300000 bounds the entire call, including all steps
chunkMs: 10000 is the maximum gap between output chunks after output starts (streaming only)
firstChunkMs separately bounds the time until the first output of each step

questions.question: One of my tools calls a slow external API. How do I give only that tool a 60-second timeout while all other tools get 10 seconds?
expected_answer: timeout: { toolMs: 10000, tools: { <toolName>Ms: 60000 } }
toolMs is the default for all tool executions; per-tool keys named {toolName}Ms inside tools take precedence

questions.question: What temperature does the AI SDK use when I don't set one? I assumed it's 0 so outputs are deterministic.
expected_answer: It is no longer 0 by default (since AI SDK 5.0); when unset, the provider/model default applies
Set temperature explicitly (or use seed where supported) for more reproducible output
The docs recommend setting either temperature or topP, not both

questions.question: What values does the top-level reasoning option accept, and what is its default?
expected_answer: Default is 'provider-default'
Other values: 'none', 'minimal', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', 'max'
Provider-specific settings take precedence over values derived from reasoning

questions.question: I passed topK to a provider that doesn't support it and nothing failed. How can I find out that the setting was ignored?
expected_answer: The SDK generates a warning instead of failing
Check the warnings property on the result

questions.question: What are the possible values of useChat's status, and what does each mean?
expected_answer: submitted: message sent, waiting for the response stream to start
streaming: response chunks are arriving
ready: response complete, a new message can be sent
error: the request failed

questions.question: How do I bind useChat's input and handleInputChange to my text field?
expected_answer: useChat no longer manages input state; input, handleInputChange and handleSubmit are not part of the current API
Keep the input in your own state (e.g. useState) and call sendMessage({ text }) on submit

questions.question: My chat UI renders message.content, but tool calls and reasoning never show up. What am I doing wrong?
expected_answer: Render message.parts, not content
Iterate the parts and switch on part.type (text, reasoning, tool-<name>, etc.)

questions.question: useChat re-renders on every token during long answers and the page becomes sluggish. How do I reduce the update frequency?
expected_answer: Use the throttle option on useChat (in milliseconds, e.g. 50)
It throttles reactive message updates in React and Vue; stream processing and callbacks stay immediate

questions.question: My chat UI just shows 'An error occurred' no matter what fails on the server. How do I show a more useful message?
expected_answer: Error messages are masked by default for security
Pass an onError function to toUIMessageStream (or createUIMessageStream) that returns the text to send to the client
Avoid forwarding sensitive internal details

questions.question: I redact errors with onError in toUIMessageStream, but some tool errors still reach the client with the raw provider message. Why?
expected_answer: Errors from provider-executed tools (providerExecuted: true) bypass the stream's error masking and its onError callback
So onError cannot be relied on to redact them

questions.question: useChat sends requests to /api/chat, but my route is /api/assistant. How do I change that?
expected_answer: Pass transport: new DefaultChatTransport({ api: '/api/assistant' })
The default endpoint is /api/chat

questions.question: How do I send only the latest message plus the chat id to my server, instead of the full history on every request?
expected_answer: Use prepareSendMessagesRequest on DefaultChatTransport
It receives { id, messages, trigger, messageId } and returns a custom body, e.g. { body: { id, message: messages.at(-1) } }
The server then loads the earlier messages itself

questions.question: My backend only returns a plain text stream. Can useChat consume it, and what do I give up?
expected_answer: Yes, with TextStreamChatTransport
Tool calls, usage and finish reasons are not available with plain text streams

questions.question: Can useChat talk to a ToolLoopAgent directly in the same process, without an HTTP API route?
expected_answer: Yes, with DirectChatTransport({ agent })

questions.question: My model produces reasoning, but the chat UI never receives any reasoning parts. What do I change on the server?
expected_answer: Pass sendReasoning: true to toUIMessageStream
Reasoning then arrives as reasoning parts (and reasoning-file); sources likewise need sendSources: true

questions.question: How do I attach the model id and token usage to each assistant message so the client can display them?
expected_answer: Use the messageMetadata callback of toUIMessageStream on the server; it receives ({ part }) and can return metadata for the start or finish part
Read it on the client from message.metadata (typed via the UIMessage generic)

questions.question: I send a PDF with sendMessage({ text, files }) and the model ignores it, while images work fine. Why?
expected_answer: Only image/* and text/* files are converted to multimodal parts automatically
Other file types such as PDF must be handled manually

questions.question: On the client, how can I tell whether a response ended because the user clicked stop, because the network dropped, or because of an error?
expected_answer: useChat's onFinish callback receives { message, messages, isAbort, isDisconnect, isError }

questions.question: In useChat's onToolCall I `await addToolOutput(...)` for a client-side tool, and the chat sometimes hangs. What's wrong?
expected_answer: Don't await addToolOutput inside onToolCall; the docs warn it can cause deadlocks
Use sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls to resubmit once all tool results are available
Check toolCall.dynamic first so addToolOutput is typed correctly

questions.question: How do I report back to the model that a client-side tool failed?
expected_answer: Call addToolOutput with tool, toolCallId, state: 'output-error' and errorText (instead of output)

questions.question: From a createUIMessageStream route, I want to send a custom 'loading' weather data part and later replace it with the result, without ending up with two separate parts in the message. How?
expected_answer: Write a custom data part (e.g. type 'data-weather') with an id using createUIMessageStream's writer
Writing another data part with the same id later updates the existing part in place on the client (reconciliation)

questions.question: I send a notification as a data part from the server. It shows up in onData, but it's missing from message.parts and isn't saved with the chat. Why?
expected_answer: The part was sent with transient: true
Transient data parts are delivered only to the onData callback and are never added to message history

questions.question: I write a custom data part in createUIMessageStream and then merge a streamText result into the same stream. How do I avoid sending a second 'start' chunk?
expected_answer: writer.merge(toUIMessageStream({ stream: result.stream, sendStart: false }))
The start part was already written before the data part

questions.question: Our backend is written in Python (FastAPI). Can it stream responses that useChat understands? What does it need to send?
expected_answer: Yes: implement the UI Message Stream protocol: Server-Sent Events whose data lines are JSON parts (start, text-start, text-delta, text-end, finish, ...)
Set the response header x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v1
End the stream with data: [DONE]

questions.question: After enabling resumable streams, clicking Stop no longer stops the model: generation continues and keeps using tokens. Why?
expected_answer: With resumable streams, client-side aborts are treated as disconnects: stop(), closing the tab or refreshing only close the HTTP connection
Actually stopping requires a dedicated stop endpoint that cancels the active work and clears activeStreamId
Avoid automatic reconnects for that chat after stopping

questions.question: What do I need on the server for useChat's resume option to work?
expected_answer: useChat({ resume: true }) sends a GET request to /api/chat/[id]/stream on mount
The POST handler creates the stream with the resumable-stream package (backed by Redis) via consumeSseStream and saves activeStreamId
The GET handler returns 204 when there is no activeStreamId, otherwise resumes the existing stream
onEnd clears activeStreamId

questions.question: I use Output.object together with tools in generateText with stopWhen: isStepCount(2), and sometimes reading result.output throws. What's going on?
expected_answer: Structured output generation counts as a step, so tool steps can use up the step budget
If the final step ends with tool-calls instead of stop, accessing result.output throws NoOutputGeneratedError (output is a getter, so destructuring throws too)
Raise the stopWhen limit to leave room for tool execution plus the output step

questions.question: How do I make the model classify a support ticket as exactly one of 'bug', 'feature' or 'question'?
expected_answer: generateText with output: Output.choice({ options: ['bug', 'feature', 'question'] })
Read the label from result.output

questions.question: I need exactly 5 items from Output.array. How do I enforce that?
expected_answer: Set minItems: 5 and maxItems: 5 (equal values require an exact count)
Both must be non-negative integers and maxItems must be at least minItems

questions.question: How do I stream each completed, validated item of a generated list one at a time?
expected_answer: Use streamText with output: Output.array({ element })
Iterate elementStream; each element is complete and validated

questions.question: With streamText and Output.array({ element, maxItems: 3 }), what happens if the model starts generating a 4th element? Is generation stopped?
expected_answer: elementStream errors before emitting the first excess element
The final output promise rejects
Provider generation is not aborted automatically

questions.question: I just need valid JSON back with no fixed schema. Which Output should I use, and does it validate the structure?
expected_answer: Output.json()
It only checks that the response is valid JSON, not its structure or value types

questions.question: When structured output fails schema validation, how do I get the raw text the model actually produced?
expected_answer: generateText throws NoObjectGeneratedError; check with NoObjectGeneratedError.isInstance(error)
error.text holds the raw text; the error also exposes response, usage and cause

questions.question: My model wraps its JSON in ```json code fences, so Output.object fails to parse it. How can I fix this without changing the prompt?
expected_answer: Wrap the model with wrapLanguageModel using extractJsonMiddleware()
It strips markdown code fences before parsing; it accepts an optional transform function

questions.question: If I pass middleware: [a, b] to wrapLanguageModel, which middleware is the outermost?
expected_answer: Middlewares are applied in array order as a(b(model)), so the first one (a) is the outermost

questions.question: My open-weights model returns its chain of thought inside <think>...</think> tags mixed into the text. How do I separate it from the answer?
expected_answer: Wrap the model with wrapLanguageModel and extractReasoningMiddleware({ tagName: 'think' })
The extracted content is exposed as reasoning; startWithReasoning: true prepends the opening tag for models that omit it

questions.question: How can I give a model alias default settings (e.g. temperature and providerOptions) everywhere it's used, without repeating them in every call?
expected_answer: Wrap the model with wrapLanguageModel and defaultSettingsMiddleware({ settings })
Register the wrapped model under an alias in customProvider's languageModels

questions.question: How do I add a default system prompt to a model that only applies when a call doesn't provide its own?
expected_answer: Use defaultInstructionsMiddleware({ instructions }) with wrapLanguageModel
It applies the default only when the call has no system message; it accepts a string, a SystemModelMessage or an array of them

questions.question: With createProviderRegistry, how do I reference a model, and can I change the character between the provider and the model id?
expected_answer: Ids look like 'provider:model' (':' is the default separator), e.g. registry.languageModel('openai:<model>')
Pass { separator: ' > ' } (any string) as the second argument to change it

questions.question: I pass model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5' as a plain string and get an authentication error, even though ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set. Why?
expected_answer: Plain model strings go through the global provider, which is the Vercel AI Gateway by default
The gateway needs AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY (or OIDC on Vercel), not the Anthropic key
Alternatively use the @ai-sdk/anthropic provider instance directly, or change the default with globalThis.AI_SDK_DEFAULT_PROVIDER

questions.question: How do I make plain model strings like 'gpt-6-astra' resolve directly through the OpenAI provider instead of the AI Gateway?
expected_answer: Set globalThis.AI_SDK_DEFAULT_PROVIDER = openai once at startup
Plain ids then resolve through that provider without a prefix

questions.question: How do I restrict my app to three approved models through a custom provider, so that any other model id fails?
expected_answer: Use customProvider with only those models in languageModels (optionally under aliases)
Don't set fallbackProvider; without it only the listed models are available

questions.question: How do I unit test a function that calls generateText without calling a real model?
expected_answer: Use MockLanguageModelV4 from 'ai/test'
Implement doGenerate returning content (e.g. [{ type: 'text', text }]), finishReason, usage and warnings

questions.question: What does the mockValues test helper do once it has returned every value in its array?
expected_answer: It keeps returning the last value

questions.question: In tests, how do I simulate a slow streaming model with a delay before the first chunk and between chunks?
expected_answer: simulateReadableStream({ chunks, initialDelayInMs, chunkDelayInMs }) imported from 'ai'
Return it from doStream as { stream }

questions.question: Write a Vitest test for a function that calls streamText, using a mock model that streams 'Hello world'.
expected_answer: new MockLanguageModelV4({ doStream: async () => ({ stream: simulateReadableStream({ chunks: [...] }) }) })
Chunks are typed events: text-start, text-delta (with delta), text-end, then a finish part with finishReason and usage
MockLanguageModelV4 comes from 'ai/test', simulateReadableStream from 'ai'

questions.question: Write a ToolLoopAgent that accepts a typed per-request option tier: 'free' | 'pro' and uses a larger model for pro users.
expected_answer: Define callOptionsSchema: z.object({ tier: z.enum(['free', 'pro']) })
prepareCall: ({ options, ...settings }) => ({ ...settings, model: options.tier === 'pro' ? <large> : <small> })
Call agent.generate({ prompt, options: { tier } }); options become required once the schema is defined

questions.question: After I added prepareCall to my agent to switch models, the agent lost its tools and instructions. Why?
expected_answer: prepareCall's return value replaces the settings for that call
Spread ...settings into the returned object to keep the defaults and override only what you need

questions.question: Does a subagent that I call from inside a tool see the parent agent's conversation history?
expected_answer: No: by default each subagent invocation starts with a fresh context
To share history, pass the messages from the tool's execute options into the subagent call; the docs advise doing this sparingly

questions.question: My parent agent's context fills up with the subagent's entire output. How do I let the parent model see only a short summary while users still see the full run?
expected_answer: Define toModelOutput on the tool that wraps the subagent to map its output to what the parent sees (e.g. the last text part)
Instruct the subagent to end with a summary so there's something useful to extract

questions.question: When a user cancels while a subagent is running, the next request fails because the history contains a tool call without a result. How do I handle this?
expected_answer: Pass the execute abortSignal to the subagent; on abort it throws AbortError, which fails the tool and stops the parent loop
On later requests convert history with convertToModelMessages(messages, { ignoreIncompleteToolCalls: true }) to drop tool calls without results

questions.question: I stream subagent progress by yielding from an async generator execute, but each yield replaces the previous output instead of appending to it. Is that expected?
expected_answer: Yes: each yield replaces the previous preliminary output
Yield the cumulative UIMessage, e.g. from readUIMessageStream over the subagent's UI message stream
On the client, output-available tool parts carry a preliminary flag until the final output arrives

questions.question: If I call a WorkflowAgent's stream() without stopWhen, is there a step limit?
expected_answer: No: stream() has no maximum step count when stopWhen is omitted
Bound it with isStepCount(n); generate() defaults to 20 steps
An answer saying WorkflowAgent has no default step limit is acceptable for stream()

questions.question: In a WorkflowAgent, how do I make a tool's execute function a durable step with automatic retries and persistence?
expected_answer: Mark the execute function with the 'use step' directive
repairToolCall and experimental_download must also be marked 'use step' inside a workflow

questions.question: Can I put my database client into runtimeContext for a WorkflowAgent?
expected_answer: No: for WorkflowAgent, runtimeContext and toolsContext must be serializable
Pass identifiers and recreate clients inside step functions

questions.question: What is the maximum number of steps a ToolLoopAgent can be configured to run?
expected_answer: The docs define no hard maximum; the default is isStepCount(20)
Raise it with isStepCount(n) or remove the limit with isLoopFinished()
Wrong if it invents a maximum

questions.question: I set toolChoice: 'none', but the model still returned a tool call. What does generateText do in that case?
expected_answer: generateText raises ToolChoiceViolationError
In streamText the tool parts are withheld, so client-side tools aren't invoked either

questions.question: Can a tool's description change depending on per-request context?
expected_answer: Yes: description can be a function that receives the tool's context (and experimental_sandbox)
It is resolved before each step

questions.question: How do I ask the provider for strictly schema-conformant tool calls for one particular tool?
expected_answer: Set strict: true on that tool()
It is off by default and ignored by providers that don't support it

questions.question: I added inputExamples to my tools, but OpenAI models don't seem to use them. Why, and how can I make them work?
expected_answer: inputExamples is natively supported only by Anthropic providers; others ignore it
Use addToolInputExamplesMiddleware to append the examples to the tool descriptions (default prefix 'Input Examples:', remove defaults to true)

questions.question: How can a long-running tool report progress to the UI before returning its final result?
expected_answer: Make execute an async generator
Earlier yields are preliminary results (status updates); the last yielded value becomes the final result

questions.question: My tool's onInputDelta callback never fires, although onInputStart and onInputAvailable do. Why?
expected_answer: onInputDelta fires only with streamText; with generateText you only get onInputStart and onInputAvailable

questions.question: My tools are loaded at runtime from a config file, so TypeScript can't know their schemas. What should I use, and how do I tell those calls apart from static ones?
expected_answer: Define them with dynamicTool; its execute input is typed unknown and must be validated at runtime
Check toolCall.dynamic to narrow dynamic vs static calls (in the UI they appear as 'dynamic-tool' parts)

questions.question: A tool grants the user a new permission mid-run. How do I make tool calls in later steps receive the updated context?
expected_answer: Tool context is treated as immutable inside tools
Inspect the previous step in prepareStep and return an updated toolsContext (runtimeContext can be updated the same way and applies to the current and later steps)

questions.question: Is runtimeContext automatically added to the prompt, so the model knows things like the user's plan tier?
expected_answer: No, runtimeContext is never added to the prompt automatically
It's also not passed to tool execute or description functions; it's visible in prepareStep, lifecycle callbacks, step results, approval callbacks and (filtered) telemetry

questions.question: I pass an API key to a tool through toolsContext. Will it show up in my OpenTelemetry traces?
expected_answer: Not by default: tool context is excluded from telemetry unless you list properties under telemetry.includeToolsContext
runtimeContext works the same way with telemetry.includeRuntimeContext
Filtering is shallow, applies only to telemetry integrations, and is not a general security boundary

questions.question: How do I keep prompts and model outputs out of my traces while still recording spans and timing?
expected_answer: Set telemetry: { recordInputs: false, recordOutputs: false } (both record by default)
Raw provider bodies and provider metadata are then omitted as well

questions.question: My tracing dashboard filters on the span name ai.generateText, but nothing shows up since I switched to the OpenTelemetry integration from @ai-sdk/otel. Why?
expected_answer: The OpenTelemetry integration uses GenAI semantic-convention span names: invoke_agent {modelId}, step {n}, chat {modelId}, execute_tool {toolName}
The old ai.* span names (ai.generateText, ai.streamText, ai.toolCall) come from LegacyOpenTelemetry

questions.question: I registered OpenTelemetry globally and passed telemetry: { integrations: [DevToolsTelemetry()] } on one call. That call disappeared from my OTel traces. Why?
expected_answer: Per-call integrations replace the globally registered integrations for that call
List both integrations on that call if you want both

questions.question: How do I open AI SDK DevTools to inspect my runs, and where does it store the captured data?
expected_answer: Register DevToolsTelemetry from @ai-sdk/devtools (via registerTelemetry or per call)
Run npx @ai-sdk/devtools@latest and open http://localhost:4983
Data is stored in plain text in .devtools/generations.json (added to .gitignore); it's for local development only

questions.question: DevTools shows my streamText runs, but the raw provider response body is always missing. How do I see it?
expected_answer: Raw request and response bodies are excluded by default in AI SDK 7
For streamText (and ToolLoopAgent.stream()) only include: { requestBody: true } is available; the response body cannot be retained
For generateText use include: { requestBody: true, responseBody: true }

sources.section: Request and response bodies excluded by default

questions.snapshot_gap: The Metrics section (gen_ai.client.inference.duration, MeterProvider) is in the live docs (2026-11-06) but not in the 2026-11-01 snapshot: neither term appears in data/corpus. Answerable only after a snapshot refresh; until then 'not in the docs' is the faithful answer. Excluded from v5 hard-set results.
questions.question: Why doesn't the gen_ai.client.inference.duration metric show up in my monitoring?
expected_answer: It requires a configured MeterProvider
LegacyOpenTelemetry doesn't emit it; the OpenTelemetry integration records it (in seconds) for generateText and streamText

questions.question: I request n: 10 images from a model that only allows 1 image per call. What happens, and can I control the batching?
expected_answer: generateImage calls the model as many times as needed, in parallel, to produce n images
The default batch size follows provider-documented per-call limits; override it with maxImagesPerCall

questions.question: I'm using a Gemini model that can output images through generateText. Where do the generated images come back?
expected_answer: In result.files
Each file has base64, uint8Array and mediaType (e.g. image/png); filter with file.mediaType.startsWith('image/')

questions.question: When an image provider blocks my prompt for moderation and returns no image, does generateImage keep retrying?
expected_answer: Unclassified empty responses are retried according to maxRetries
Providers can mark terminal empty responses such as moderation blocks with isRetryable: false, which skips retries
The failure surfaces as NoImageGeneratedError

questions.question: Can rerank work with JSON objects instead of strings, and how do I get the best-matching object back?
expected_answer: Yes, documents can be strings or JSON objects
result.rerankedDocuments[0] is the top document; ranking contains originalIndex, score and document

questions.question: I use smoothStream and Japanese answers arrive in big, uneven bursts instead of flowing smoothly. How do I fix it?
expected_answer: The default word chunking doesn't work well for languages without spaces between words (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Thai)
Pass chunking: new Intl.Segmenter('ja', { granularity: 'word' })

questions.question: What delay does smoothStream use between chunks by default, and how do I turn the delay off?
expected_answer: delayInMs defaults to 10 ms
Set delayInMs: null to disable delays (they are also skipped while the document is hidden)
It is passed through streamText's experimental_transform option

questions.question: Write a Next.js route handler that streams a chat response to useChat with reasoning and sources enabled, replacing any error details with 'Something went wrong'.
expected_answer: Call streamText with the converted UI messages (convertToModelMessages)
return createUIMessageStreamResponse({ stream: toUIMessageStream({ stream: result.stream, sendReasoning: true, sendSources: true, onError: () => 'Something went wrong' }) })

questions.question: Why is response.body empty on my generateText result in v7, and how do I get it back?
expected_answer: Request and response bodies are excluded by default in v7
Opt in with include: { requestBody: true, responseBody: true }
For streamText only requestBody is available

sources.section: Request and response bodies excluded by default

expected_answer: system -> instructions
experimental_include -> include
onStepFinish -> onStepEnd
onFinish -> onEnd
result.fullStream -> result.stream

questions.question: How long do resumable streams stay in Redis before they expire?
expected_answer: The docs only say the expiry is set by the resumable-stream package; no duration is given. The bot must not invent a number

questions.question: What is the maximum file size I can attach with sendMessage({ files })?
expected_answer: Not documented. The bot must not borrow unrelated limits such as the DevTools 5 MiB media preview limit

questions.question: How long does AI SDK DevTools keep captured runs before deleting them?
expected_answer: Not documented. Data is stored in .devtools/generations.json, but no retention period is given

questions.question: Which provider behind the AI Gateway is the cheapest for Claude models?
expected_answer: Not in the docs. The bot must not name a provider as cheapest

questions.question: How many requests per minute can I send through the AI Gateway before I get rate limited?
expected_answer: Not in the AI SDK docs. The bot must not invent a limit
